name: piladb
tagline: Go REST database whose only data structure is the stack: PUSH, POP and PEEK JSON values in named stacks.
description: piladb is a lightweight in-memory database engine in Go whose only data structure is the stack ('pila' is Spanish for stack). You create databases and named stacks through a REST API, then push, pop, peek, size or flush JSON values of any type, with the top element always available in constant time; stacks grow until they hit host or configured limits. It ships as a single self-contained binary configured over the API or CLI flags, and was written by Fernando Álvarez in Madrid. The last tagged release is v0.2.0-alpha from April 2018 and the main branch has not moved since; it is a neat teaching project in API-first database design rather than a production store.
statusNote: No commits on the main branch since March 2018 (v0.2.0-alpha); unmaintained.

scale.notes: In-memory only; capacity bounded by host RAM or configured limits.

strengths: Dead-simple stack semantics with constant-time access to the top element
Clean REST API and single static binary
weaknesses: In-memory only: data is lost on restart
useCases: Teaching REST API and database design
Throwaway LIFO work stacks in prototypes
